summary: One shared library with a plain C ABI over the CUDA entries (stored-tile GEMMs, recurrent layers and recovery, FP8 KV attention, token sampling, greedy accept) and a standard-library ctypes loader, so a Python engine calls them on its own buffers and streams without writing an extension
implementation_scope: crit_inference.h declares 74 extern "C" functions: stored-tile-gemm's plans (opaque 64-byte host buffers), repacks, W8A8 / W4A4 GEMMs, decode GEMVs and BF16-activation GEMMs, plain and gated; recurrent-layer-kernels' conv1d (plain and deferred), gated-delta prefill, columns and deferred columns, and Mamba-2 SSD prefill and columns with their scratch sizes; recurrent-state-recovery's verify, select, recompute, deferred verify and (grouped) record_accepted; fp8-kv-attention's BF16 / FP32 writes at host or device positions, prefill (BF16 or E4M3 queries) and decode with windows, sinks, soft-caps and tree masks; token-sampling's select, mask, sample, verify, logprobs and commit with Params and Request rows packed on the host; device-speculative-round's greedy accept, truncate, pack, budget, seed and packed layout; mapped pinned host memory and stream synchronization. crit_inference.cpp rebuilds each entry's C++ argument structs and forwards the call; the crit_inference_python CMake target links it with the entries' sources (crit_* symbols exported only). crit_inference.py reads every declaration from the header to give the functions their ctypes types, raises CudaError on a nonzero status and adds plan, Request / Params row, packed-layout, mapped-memory and file-read helpers. Model-specific kernels (norms, rotary embedding, gates, embeddings) stay in the engine.

agent_guidance.use_when: The engine's forward pass is driven from Python (PyTorch or another array library owns the buffers and streams) and it uses several of the bound CUDA entries
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The engine is native C++ (link the entries directly), it needs one of the entries' C++-only extension points (templates, custom epilogues), or it already compiles its own extension around the same calls and measures no difference
provides: A C ABI whose arguments are integers, floats and pointers only: device addresses from data_ptr(), streams from cuda_stream, no Python headers or interpreter version in the build
One shared library target (crit_inference_python) with the bound entries' sources and only the crit_* symbols exported
A ctypes loader with no signature table of its own: every function's types come from the shipped header, so a call cannot disagree with the C declaration
CudaError carrying the function name and cudaError_t code for any refused or failed launch
Opaque plan buffers filled once at load and passed to every launch, with the plan's scratch sizes returned
Request and Params rows packed on the host from keyword arguments, plus their sizes and position offsets
Pinned, device-mapped host memory and a file reader straight into it (for tables kept in host memory)
engine_supplies: Device buffers, their dtypes, alignment and lifetimes (the library keeps no pointer between calls)
The CUDA stream of every launch and graph capture around the calls
Plans for its shapes, scratch allocated from the returned sizes, and copies of packed rows to device memory
Every model-specific kernel and the forward pass itself
preserve: Each function forwards to its entry unchanged: the entries' contracts, failure codes and bitwise properties hold as documented there
The header is the one signature table; change it and crit_inference.cpp together and keep CRIT_INFERENCE_ABI in step with crit_inference.py
Plan buffers are copies of the entries' plans: plan once for the shapes and device that launch them
adapt: Bind another entry by declaring it in crit_inference.h, forwarding it in crit_inference.cpp and adding its sources to the target
Build for the device's exact architecture (CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a on an RTX 5090) so the NVFP4 MMA is compiled; st_fp4_mma_compiled() reports it
Wrap the raw calls in the engine's own tensor-aware layer when that keeps the forward pass readable

code_files.purpose: The C ABI: every exported function, its argument order and the ABI version
Forwarding of each C function to its entry's C++ interface
ctypes loader typed from the header, CudaError, plan, row, layout and host-memory helpers

requires.hardware: The bound entries' devices (CUDA C++20, sm_80+; the NVFP4 W4A4 GEMM needs an sm_120a / sm_121a build); CUDA 13.1+ toolkit to build; Python 3.11+ standard library to load
requires.model: Any model whose engine uses the bound entries from Python
requires.workload: Python-driven forward passes, eager or captured into CUDA graphs on the engine's streams

contract.input: Integer device addresses, integer cudaStream_t handles, scalar arguments and host plan / row buffers, in the header's argument order
contract.output: The entries' outputs in the caller's buffers; the entry's cudaError_t, raised as CudaError by the loader when nonzero
contract.ownership: The caller owns every buffer and stream; the library allocates only on crit_host_alloc_mapped and frees only on crit_host_free
contract.failure: Null plan, row or offset buffers and activation codes outside 0-2 return cudaErrorInvalidValue before forwarding; everything else is the entry's own validation and launch error; the loader refuses a missing library file with its path and an ABI version other than its own
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; token sampling links Core's draw (crit::core) as the entry does

dependencies: The stored-tile-gemm, recurrent-layer-kernels, recurrent-state-recovery, fp8-kv-attention, token-sampling and device-speculative-round sources
CUDA runtime; crit::core for token sampling
Python standard library (ctypes) for the loader

validation.host: Every header declaration has a C++ definition with the same return and argument types, the header's ABI version and plan size equal the loader's, a missing library is refused with its path and the build target, and file reads into host memory are exact and refuse short files (tests/test_inference_bindings.py)
validation.native: tests/inference/python_bindings_check.py (ctest crit_inference_python) loads the built library and checks every declared function is exported, greedy select and sample through packed Params and Request rows (lowest id on ties, positions advanced), grouped and single record_accepted, and a refused launch raised as CudaError with its code; passed on an RTX 5090 (sm_120a build, CUDA 13.1, WSL2), where the library exports exactly the 74 crit_* functions and reports the NVFP4 MMA compiled
validation.performance: No claim; a call adds ctypes argument conversion on the host (microseconds) and nothing inside CUDA graphs
